description: I hope we will do well
summary: Project Cosmia is a public web tool that lets anyone watch a patch of sky change over time in NASA’s SPHEREx data. You enter Right Ascension and declination, or pick a preset such as Barnard’s Star, Epsilon Indi B, WISE 0855, RW Aurigae or R Draconis. The tool shows the patch as a short blinking sequence, so moving objects like brown dwarfs, nearby stars, comets and asteroids stand out. You can choose the field of view and any of the six detector bands. A stacked mode averages the bands to reduce noise, difference and sum modes highlight motion, and a spectrum and light curve update when you click a position. The page can be queried through URL parameters for embedding. A Python backend fetches real SPHEREx cutouts from NASA’s IRSA archive; without it the page runs on a simulated demo sky. Cosmia makes SPHEREx discoveries easier for volunteers to find.
details:
• What it does: Cosmia turns SPHEREx spectral images into a blink comparator. A Python server (Flask, Astropy, astroquery, SciPy) queries IRSA for every SPHEREx image covering your coordinates, downloads small cutouts, and resamples them onto one sky grid with north up. The browser then plays the frames as a video. Averaging the bands within each survey improves signal-to-noise, and the spectrum plot uses the wavelength measured at the target in each frame. Frame metadata shows the flagged-pixel fraction.
  • Benefit and impact: it lets non-experts spot motion by eye, the way volunteers found many comets and brown dwarfs with earlier tools.
  • Tools: HTML/CSS/JavaScript canvas front end, Python, Flask, Astropy, astroquery, SciPy, NumPy.
  • Creative choices: a calm pastel interface, and a path overlay showing where a known mover should be so users learn what motion looks like.
  • Limits: demo mode is simulated, with proper motions taken from published values. Gaia and WISE overlays are not yet implemented.
